avis.comment: Problem statement keeps only background, prior work and open questions; the paper's own approach, datasets and results are removed. Classification: the paper has no theorems, proofs or formal analysis (equations only describe the method and prior frameworks), so experiments_only fits better than mostly_experiments. Data mix (four synthetic families dominating ablations, two real datasets) supports mostly_synthetic; domains are fine. All 12 quotes match the paper exactly and support their targets. The ~1,300 A100 GPU-hour estimate is a plausible order of magnitude given ~12h per synthetic run, many ablation runs and no reported total.

avis.comment: Statement keeps to background, prior work and open questions; the flow-model paragraph points toward initial-noise correction but only through prior-work facts (exact reversal, 2-rectification suffering when reversed noise is non-Gaussian), so no forbidden reveal. The 4,500 GPU-hour estimate is a plausible order of magnitude given ~0.75M SDv2 768px samples, LoRA runs, DDPO sweeps and two 256px pixel-space flow models trained from scratch.

Core approach of Theorem 1 / Remark 1 (reference model near initialization); exact quote.
Key technical device of Remark 3 / Lemma 16 (covering of the input sphere, only log of cover size enters); exact quote.
Smooth-loss Rademacher bound (Lemma 1) plus near-linearity of the iterate class (Remark 2, Lemma 22); exact quote supports it.
Paper explicitly shows the recursive layer-wise estimate yields C^L factors; exact quote; a plausible main approach a plan could take.
Exact quote; stability analyses relying on smooth activations do not cover ReLU, as stated in the Introduction.

The paper's own method is itself a capacity-based Rademacher bound over a fixed, data-independent hypothesis space (W_1), refined with a smooth-loss bound; the paper does not show this family fails, only that standard versions usually give 1/sqrt(n). The target conflicts with F3, so a reader could not tell whether a Rademacher-based plan pursues it.
